correctness.rationale: For a nest of \(s\) internal edges, connectedness in a tree gives exactly \(s+1\) induced internal vertices, so the published standard-weight facet height is \( inom{s+1}{2}\). The affine total is \( inom n2\), forcing the uniform point \(n\mathbf1/2\). At that point the facet slack is \(s(n-1-s)/2\), while the intrinsic subset-normal norm is \(\sqrt{s(n-1-s)/(n-1)}\), yielding the exact shell formula. Its minimum occurs at \(s=1\) or \(s=n-2\). Singleton facets \(x_e\ge1\) give a matching all-center radius upper bound when summed, and equality forces every center coordinate equal, proving uniqueness.

value.rationale: Operahedra form a recent operadic family ranging continuously in combinatorial complexity from associahedra to permutahedra. The theorem identifies a metric rigidity invisible from that changing face structure: every standard realization with the same number of internal tree vertices has not only the same inradius but the same cardinality-indexed center-to-facet shell radii. This is a full-family structural metric statement, with exact contact classification, rather than a single endpoint recomputation.
